# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalent)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QH (Cave 1), Col. 2 | **Condition:** Heavily damaged

---

**2:1** [...] the gates of death [...] and the doorways of [...]

**2:2** [...] its bars are locked forever [...] with no way out [...]

**2:3** [...] the traps of the grave [...] have closed around me [...]

**2:4** [...] and the nets of death [...] have caught me [...]

**2:5** [...] the floodwaters of Belial [...] have swept over [...]

**2:6** [...] all their currents upon [...] a raging fire [...]

**2:7** [...] and their streams reach out to [...] destroy the trees [...]

**2:8** [...] green and withered alike [...] devouring everything [...]

**2:9** [...] with tongues of fire [...] until nothing remains [...]

**2:10** [...] consuming even the clay foundations [...] the parched earth [...]

**2:11** [...] those who peddle easy answers [...] have turned against me [...]

**2:12** [...] the teachers of lies [...] have hemmed me in [...]

**2:13** [...] and they have pressed in on every side [...] like the thunder of crashing waves [...]

**2:14** [...] and their surf has thrown up [...] mud and slime [...]

**2:15** [...] and I — my heart dissolved [...] like wax near a flame [...]

**2:16** [...] and my knees gave way like water [...] spilling down a hillside [...]

**2:17** [...] and I thought, I am trapped [...] in the net of [...]

**2:18** [...] judgment is coming [...] and Your correction [...]

**2:19** [...] and my suffering has exploded [...] like labor pains [...]

**2:20** [...] heading toward destruction and the grave [...] agonizing on the bed of [...]

**2:21** [...] and they tossed my soul about like a boat in the deep ocean [...]

**2:22** [...] and like a walled city [...] under siege [...]

**2:23** [...] and I writhed in pain like a first-time mother in labor [...]

**2:24** [...] for her contractions have begun [...] with excruciating pain [...]

**2:25** [...] on the birthing chair [...] for new life emerges at the threshold of death [...]

**2:26** [...] and the woman carrying a son is racked with agony [...]

**2:27** [...] for through the deathly waves she will deliver a boy [...]

**2:28** [...] and from the chains of the grave there will emerge [...] a wonder of a counselor in all his power [...]

**2:29** [...] and a man will be rescued from the waves [...] through the one who carries him [...]

**2:30** [...] all the waves [...] and the surf crashes down [...]

**2:31** [...] You held me up, O God [...] against the floodwaters [...]

**2:32** [...] and in Your faithful love [...] You kept me standing [...]

**2:33** [...] You planted my feet [...] on solid rock [...]

**2:34** [...] an eternal road [...] and trustworthy paths [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 2 is heavily damaged but contains extraordinary imagery. The birth-pangs passage (2:23-29) is one of the most debated sections in the Dead Sea Scrolls — is this a messianic birth? The "wonderful counselor" language from Isaiah 9:6 makes the connection hard to ignore. "Those who seek smooth things" is rendered dynamically as "those who peddle easy answers" to capture the contemptuous tone.*
